verdict_reason: Type and role values match the address-book API enum, but rolesOf mispredicts its return value and AddressRoles collides with addressRoles.

todos.issue: rolesOf(address) reads as 'the roles of an address' (an AddressRole[]) but returns an object { roles } picked from the address, so callers write expect(rolesOf(saved)).toEqual(heldAsConsignor) (addresses-add-handshake.spec.ts:93, address-book-edit.spec.ts:67) comparing against an AddressRoles shape. The name mispredicts the value it returns.
todos.fix: Must: the helper's name says it returns the address's roles field as an AddressRoles object (or it returns the array and callers compare arrays). One way: rename to pickRoles / rolesPartOf, or return roles and compare against heldAsConsignor.roles; consider moving the helper out of a constants module into test support beside its callers.

todos.issue: Two concepts share one name differing only by case: addressRoles (line 9) is the map of every role value, while AddressRoles (line 20) is the { roles } shape one address holds. Specs import both side by side (addresses-add-handshake.spec.ts:10-18 imports addressRoles and type AddressRoles), so a reader cannot tell from the name which one they have; the pattern elsewhere in the file (addressTypes/AddressType, addressRoles/AddressRole) leads a reader to expect AddressRoles to be the type of addressRoles.
todos.fix: Must: the { roles } shape has a name distinct from the role-value map. One way: rename the interface to HeldRoles (matching the heldAs* constants typed with it) and update AddressDocument and the specs that import it.
